name: bonk-sir-a3-sunrise
notes: Sir Bonk air.3 (anim.bonk.a3), 2026-10-22. The owner approved aerial partners for all four grounded normals and chose new timings, then approved their shapes and clocks ('looks good'). Air.1 and air.2 are accepted and integrated. This is one KEYS-ONLY pass for aerial Sunrise: a low-to-high front scoop continuing overhead. Fixed first contact 20, active 20-33 inclusive, recovery 34-53, end/free 54; landing lag 18, early auto-cancel 0-3, late auto-cancel 46. No live gameplay, binding or cook changes before animation acceptance.
character: Sir Bonk: a huge good-hearted self-appointed knight, bucket helm and broom crest, cream tabard, pot-lid pauldrons, bedsheet cape, wooden plank greatsword. 68 joints, Humanoid body with Mixamo names and full fingers; cape chains Cape_L/C/R1..4 stay at rest because the game drives them. Weapon0 is the 2.26 m plank on his right hand, with bladeHilt/bladeEnd anchors around its 1.42 m blade.
description:
Airborne Sunrise: the aerial partner of ground.3, one rising TWO-HANDED slice. He lowers the plank beside his right hip, scoops through the space in front of him and carries a broad rainbow up over his head toward the right-shoulder carry. The owner approved this shape and a 54-tick clock. Squire's Cut is the fast diagonal check, Barn Door is the wide flat sweep, and Sunrise catches space above him. No spin, somersault, gag, extra slash or imaginary foot plant.

The arc is the move. The plank itself will be the hitbox during ticks 20-33. It must travel through front, up and over throughout that window; do not park it vertically above his head for most of the active time. Ground Sunrise's early attempts failed because they kept a narrow arm-only arc and too little body turn. Reuse the accepted rainbow's torso drive, adapting every grounded stride/pivot to compact airborne leg counterbalance. The reference images show a grounded move: do not copy planted feet, its squat or its long idle tail. Option A in the arc-options image is the accepted rainbow idea; ignore the old grounded clock printed there.

Entry and exit are the actual fall reference at tick 0, never his grounded idle. The right knee starts raised, left leg hangs, left hand balances freely and plank rises back over the right shoulder. Keep the actor root fixed and ordinary movement/gravity rules unchanged: no extra lift, hang, forced dive or root travel. The hips may shift a little locally. Both legs visibly counterbalance the scoop and overhead stretch; they never plant. Cape_L/C/R1..4 stay at rest for the runtime spring.

Fixed 60 Hz clock: first contact 20, active 20-33 inclusive, recovery 34-53, free/end 54. Exact fall at 0 and from 46 through 54. Story poses:
- 0: exact fall reference tick 0.
- 5: the left hand joins a loose second grip. Bring the plank forward/upright outside the right shoulder, with the handle clear of the bucket, torso and raised knee. Both hands approximately on the handle; elbows do not wing beside his face.
- 12: low load. Chest coils roughly 40-55 degrees right, hips less. Both hands lower beside and in front of the right hip, with the blade pointing forward/down, tip well ahead and below the hilt. The raised knee tucks or shifts aside so the handle and blade have a clear outside route. No deep grounded squat or plunge of the whole fighter.
- 18: uncoil. Hips have begun unwinding first; the chest follows. Both hands lead up and forward from the right hip; plank still slopes down-forward and trails the hands. The legs counterbalance rather than hanging unchanged through the stroke.
- 20: first contact in front, not already parked overhead. The plank is roughly horizontal, tip at least 1.2 m ahead of hips, hands reaching in front of the chest. Body drive has turned the chest toward the front. Elbows down and wrists aligned, with room between handle and belly.
- 26: overhead. The rising arc passes near vertical above and a little to the right of his head, both hands up outside the bucket's right edge. Hips/chest keep unwinding left and the body opens into the stretch. Tip is well above the head; keep the hands/forearms away from crossing the face. For an overhead grip, elbows='hands' is available so an artificial downward elbow constraint does not fold the wrists.
- 33: end of the overhead arc, still moving. The blade has carried past vertical toward the back/right shoulder, tip behind the hips and still above head/hilt, without a full-body spin or stabbing into the cape. Both hands stay outside the bucket as the chest finishes its leftward turn. Do not repeat the tick-26 upright pose here: this key must complete the rainbow.
- 39: return. He reins the plank into the outside-right shoulder carry, both hands still helping, body beginning to undo the turn. No new slash or face crossing. The left hand may release after this key to reopen in balance.
- 46: exact fall reference tick 0, arms and legs restored for late auto-cancel.
- 54: same exact fall pose, free to act.

Hands: the owner accepted a loose, approximate side-by-side grip, the left fist about 8-16 cm below the right. Do not force a mirrored exact grip that crosses forearms or wings the elbows. Use two_hand_grip(..., hold='loose', elbows=True) for low/front poses, and consider elbows='hands' overhead. Solve each key from a neighbouring solution. A hilt request is soft: default hilt_weight=0.3 pulled Barn Door's hilt back into the body despite farther-out requests; weighting it at 2.0 solved that case. Measure the achieved hilt, elbow and hand positions instead of assuming the request was met. Keep the left hand approximately on the handle and allow natural turn/slide; do not cure contact warnings by making it float. Keep the blade, handle, gauntlets and forearms clear of bucket, crest, pot-lid pauldrons, torso and knees. Preserve anatomical hinges and report wrist/limit compromises.

KEY BLOCKING only. Author the listed story poses; plain interpolation is sufficient between them. Do not spend this round on breakdowns, overlap or polished transitions. The carry helper can maintain a provisional loose grip if needed for checking, but do not reshape the key intent to clear motion scores. Inspect profile, front, rear three-quarter on the striking side and gameplay. Save a changed loadable result early, run the FULL default key-pose check, and inspect affected hand/overhead close-ups.

Before delivery, measure and inspect the provisional weapon arc with genra.hitarc against defender-hurtboxes.json in scratch, radius 0.5 and active 20-33, calibration bonk. This is an approximate diagnostic using a grounded fit, not a cooked guarantee. Report total/front/back grid coverage and what the arc image shows. The owner cares most about the moving weapon coverage: do not sacrifice the front-to-overhead path to make a pretty isolated overhead pose. One key take only; owner review precedes motion. No Unity, source package, binding or cooked edits.

fixed: Owner approved: 54 ticks at 60 Hz; first hit 20, active 20-33 inclusive, recovery 34-53, end/free 54.
Exact fall at 0 and 46-54 for the airborne handoff.
Gameplay planning notes: landing lag 18, auto-cancel 0-3 and from 46; live values wait for animation acceptance.
One rising two-handed front-to-overhead arc; no actor-root travel or added hover/dive.
adjustable: Pose amplitude, compact airborne counterbalance and exact arc within approved shape and story times.
Do not retime contact, active, handoff or free ticks without owner feedback.
